The test therefore exercises the real renderer with a record shape persist_slice would reject, so it proves the collapse-and-truncate behaviour but not that a production-shaped record renders the same way. Behaviour under test is unaffected today because render_escalation reads every field through .get() and _ordered_options tolerates a missing list (verified by running the module: 22 tests OK, and the rendered `- Context: ` line measures 411 chars = 11-char prefix + the 400-char budget).

P3: The helper's docstring spends four of its five lines narrating the deleted re-implementation rather than describing what the helper returns. The historical claim is accurate today (the removed body was `" ".join(filled.split())[:CRASH_CONTEXT_RENDER_LIMIT - 1]` — collapse correct, unconditional slice wrong, no ellipsis wrong, i.e. two of _one_line's three behaviours), but it is a claim about code that no longer exists anywhere in the tree and no future reader can check it. The repo's convention is decision-justifying comments; this is closer to a changelog entry, which belongs in the commit body (where it already is, in 7edd648).

escalations.question: Retry this slice, skip it and continue the run, or stop the run to diagnose the exception?

options.label: Retry this slice
options.detail: Recommended default. The CONTROLLER must act on this at the next dispatch: re-dispatch the wave on this slice, keeping the committed work on its branch.

options.label: Skip this slice
options.detail: The CONTROLLER must act on this at the next dispatch: leave the slice ESCALATED and dispatch only the independent slices. Nothing in the loop enforces a skip — the default re-dispatch procedure would retry it.

options.label: Stop the run
options.detail: The CONTROLLER must act on this at the next dispatch: halt the run instead of dispatching another wave, so the exception can be diagnosed before more agents are spent. Nothing in the loop stops the run by itself.
